product_description: Judges whether a sent-but-unanswered email genuinely warrants a follow-up nudge, for a Strategic Partnership Manager. Runs once per new sent message with no reply yet, on gpt-4o-mini.

dimensions.name: H1: Warranted-Judgment Accuracy
dimensions.question: Does warranted=true only fire for a real single-recipient/small-group ask expecting a reply?
dimensions.low: Broadcasts, self-sent notes, doc-drops with no ask, or already-resolved topics marked warranted=true; or a real unanswered ask wrongly marked false.
dimensions.medium: Correct verdict but for a borderline case where the reasoning shows it was a close call.
dimensions.high: warranted=true reserved for genuine asks awaiting reply; false correctly catches broadcasts, self-notes, and already-scheduled touchpoints.

dimensions.name: Ho1: Why-Specificity
dimensions.question: Does "why" cite actual content from the message rather than a generic day-count justification?
dimensions.low: "why" is just the day-count ("no reply in N days") with nothing about what the message actually said.
dimensions.medium: "why" references the general topic but not the specific line that actually decided the verdict.
dimensions.high: "why" quotes or paraphrases the exact detail (an ask, a resolving line, a recipient list) that drove the verdict.

dimensions.name: Ha1: Redundant-Nudge Risk
dimensions.question: Does it catch messages that already say the topic will be resolved another way (e.g. "we'll cover this on the call")?
dimensions.low: Message explicitly states the topic is already being resolved elsewhere, but this is missed and warranted=true anyway — would nudge a contact about something already scheduled.
dimensions.medium: Catches the resolved-elsewhere signal but the why doesn't clearly explain it.
dimensions.high: Any already-scheduled-touchpoint or administrative/templated content is correctly excluded from a nudge, with the resolving detail named in why.

test_cases.label: BAD
test_cases.input_description: Message sent to a distribution list of three addresses sharing a pricing sheet, explicitly says no action needed.
test_cases.ground_truth: warranted=false — broadcast to a distro list, explicit no-action-needed statement, not a single-recipient ask.

evals.warranted_accuracy: FAIL — marked warranted=true despite being a broadcast with an explicit no-action-needed line.
evals.why_specificity: FAIL — why is just the day count, ignores the message content entirely.
evals.redundant_nudge_risk: FAIL — the "no action needed" line is a clear resolved/non-actionable signal that was missed.

candidate_input.subject: Updated pricing sheet attached
candidate_input.body: Hi all, attaching the latest pricing sheet for reference. No action needed right now — just keeping everyone in the loop.

candidate_output.why: It's been 6 business days with no reply.

test_cases.label: AVERAGE
test_cases.input_description: Single recipient asked to review redlines, but the message itself already offers to cover it on Thursday's call.
test_cases.ground_truth: warranted=false — the message already states the topic will be resolved on Thursday's call; nudging again would be redundant.

evals.warranted_accuracy: PASS — correctly false, since a call is already scheduled to cover it.
evals.why_specificity: PARTIAL — why says "this doesn't seem urgent," without naming the actual resolving line.
evals.redundant_nudge_risk: PARTIAL — right call, but doesn't clearly cite the Thursday-call detail as the reason.

candidate_input.subject: Contract redlines — can you take a look
candidate_input.body: Hi Marcus, sent over the redlined MSA — take a look when you get a chance. We can also just discuss it on our call Thursday if that's easier.

test_cases.label: GOOD
test_cases.input_type: Genuine single-recipient ask, no resolution offered
test_cases.input_description: Single recipient asked to confirm a specific decision (term length), nothing in the thread suggests it's being resolved elsewhere.
test_cases.ground_truth: warranted=true — real ask, single recipient, no alternate resolution stated, no reply yet.

evals.warranted_accuracy: PASS — genuine single-recipient ask with nothing resolving it elsewhere.
evals.why_specificity: PASS — names the exact ask (24mo vs 36mo confirmation) driving the verdict.
evals.redundant_nudge_risk: PASS — correctly finds no already-scheduled touchpoint, so a nudge is legitimately warranted.

candidate_input.subject: Confirming 24mo vs 36mo pricing
candidate_input.body: Hi Priya, wanted to check in — were you able to confirm with your steering committee whether you're leaning toward the 24-month or 36-month term? Happy to send more detail on either.

candidate_output.why: Ellen asked Priya to confirm the 24- vs 36-month term for the steering committee, and nothing since has addressed that ask.
